text:
{
  "claims": [
    {
      "anchor": "If you increment a counter 100 times, the AOF holds 100 entries",
      "claim_text": "Incrementing a counter 100 times results in 100 entries in the AOF.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P3.S1", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Passage states 100 entries in AOF for 100 increments."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "99 of them are unnecessary",
      "claim_text": "99 of the 100 AOF entries are unnecessary.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P3.S2", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Passage explicitly says 99 entries are not needed."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "after a rewrite that key can be rebuilt from a single command",
      "claim_text": "After an AOF rewrite, the key can be rebuilt from a single command.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P4.S1", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Rewrite writes shortest sequence; for a single key that is one command."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "On Redis 2.2 you have to run BGREWRITEAOF yourself",
      "claim_text": "On Redis 2.2, you must run BGREWRITEAOF manually.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P4.S2", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Passage says with Redis 2.2 you need to run BGREWRITEAOF from time to time."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "Redis 2.6 can trigger log rewriting automatically",
      "claim_text": "Redis 2.6 can trigger log rewriting automatically.",
      "kind": "version",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P4.S3", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": {"kind": "version", "left": "2.6", "op": ">=", "right": "2.4"},
      "reasoning": "Passage says since Redis 2.4 automatic rewriting is possible; 2.6 >= 2.4."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "Redis 2.4 and later never run an AOF rewrite and an RDB snapshot at the same time",
      "claim_text": "Redis 2.4 and later never run an AOF rewrite and an RDB snapshot simultaneously.",
      "kind": "version",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P7.S0", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": {"kind": "version", "left": "2.4", "op": ">=", "right": "2.4"},
      "reasoning": "Passage says Redis >= 2.4 avoids triggering AOF rewrite during RDB snapshot or BGSAVE during AOF rewrite."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "if you request BGREWRITEAOF while a snapshot is running, Redis schedules it and starts it once the snapshot completes",
      "claim_text": "If BGREWRITEAOF is requested during a snapshot, Redis schedules it and starts it after the snapshot completes.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P8.S0", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Passage states exactly this behavior."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "With appendfsync everysec you can lose up to one second of writes",
      "claim_text": "With appendfsync everysec, you can lose up to one second of writes.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P5.S4", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Passage says you may lose 1 second of data with everysec."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "with appendfsync always no writes are lost in any failure scenario",
      "claim_text": "With appendfsync always, no writes are lost in any failure scenario.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": false,
      "evidence": [],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Passage says 'very safe' but does not guarantee zero loss in any failure scenario."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "RDB forks less often than AOF does",
      "claim_text": "RDB forks less often than AOF does.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P1.S5", "rel": "refutes"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Passage says AOF also needs to fork() but less frequently, so AOF forks less often than RDB."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "When both AOF and RDB are enabled, Redis rebuilds the dataset from the AOF on restart rather than from the RDB file",
      "claim_text": "When both AOF and RDB are enabled, Redis uses the AOF to reconstruct the dataset on restart.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P9.S0", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Passage states AOF file will be used to reconstruct the original dataset."
    }
  ]
}
